rows.title: Interaction of β-Caryophyllene with a Simplified Membrane Model and Its Growth-Inhibitory Effect Against Escherichia coli ATCC 25922.
rows.evidence_boundary: Antibacterial and membrane-interaction findings are in vitro/model-system evidence; they do not establish therapeutic efficacy, achievable exposure, or safety in humans.

rows.title: In Silico Exploration of Cannabidiol Interactions with Outer Membrane Proteins in Salmonella Typhimurium LT2.
rows.evidence_boundary: The findings are computational docking predictions without direct biological validation; they should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of antimicrobial efficacy.

rows.title: Subchronic Exposure to Low-Dose Cannabidiol (CBD) and Δ(9)-Tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ(9)-THC) Nanoemulsions Suggests Low Renal Toxicity: A Preliminary Study.
rows.evidence_boundary: Renal safety findings come from a short-duration rat study using specific nanoemulsions and doses; they cannot establish long-term human renal safety or generalize to other formulations.

rows.title: Safety of cannabidiol isolated from Cannabis sativa L. as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283.
rows.evidence_boundary: This EFSA novel-food assessment is product- and use-condition-specific and explicitly identifies data gaps; it is not a blanket safety determination for all CBD products or populations.

rows.title: Safety of Cannabis sativaL. extract as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283.
rows.evidence_boundary: This EFSA assessment applies to a defined multi-cannabinoid extract, proposed intake, and adult target population; conclusions do not automatically transfer to other extracts, doses, or vulnerable groups.
